result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.percolation_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute percolation centrality for all nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L15147-L15242){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.percolation_centrality( states=None, weight=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Percolation centrality measures the importance of nodes based on the proportion of 'percolated paths' that pass through them. This is particularly useful for analyzing information or disease spreading in networks. When all nodes have percolation state = `1.0`, this reduces to standard betweenness centrality. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [states]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[int, float] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Dictionary mapping node labels to percolation states (values between `0.0` and `1.0`). States represent the probability of a node being in the "percolated" state (e.g., infected, informed). If `None`, all nodes default to state `1.0`. [weight]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge attribute name for weights. Currently not implemented. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of node attribute to store results. If `None`, uses `percolation_centrality`. Only used when `return_dict=False`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dict mapping node labels to percolation centrality. If `False`, stores results as node attributes and returns self. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict or Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=True`, returns `{node_label: centrality_value}`. If `return_dict=False`, returns self with node attributes set. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Basic usage with default states: ::: {#38baf6c7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_path_graph(5) pc = graph.percolation_centrality(return_dict=True) ``` ::: With custom percolation states (e.g., infection probabilities): ::: {#3142348e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_path_graph(5) states = {"1": 1.0, "2": 0.5, "3": 0.8, "4": 0.3, "5": 1.0} pc = graph.percolation_centrality(states=states, return_dict=True) ``` :::
